groups.problem: Bigin passes the credential ID instead of the owner's user ID to refreshOAuthTokens.
groups.rationale: All four identify the same incorrect argument, which becomes calcomUserId and also incorrectly enables user synchronization for team credentials.

groups.problem: The synchronization branch returns a native fetch Response to callers expecting decoded tokens or Axios/Gaxios response objects.
groups.rationale: All five report the same return-contract mismatch in refreshOAuthTokens. The different provider failures are consequences of that shared mismatch.

groups.problem: The minimum token schema uses stringified Zod schemas as literal property names, causing actual expiry and other token fields to be stripped.
groups.rationale: All four identify the same malformed schema and loss of undeclared response fields. S11 emphasizes the documented contract, but reports the same underlying behavior.

groups.problem: Google persists the safeParse result envelope as the credential key instead of its parsed data.
groups.rationale: All five flag the same assignment and resulting loss of top-level credential fields, including when synchronization is disabled.

groups.problem: The parser substitutes a literal refresh token when the response omits one, overwriting valid saved refresh tokens.
groups.rationale: Both report the same fabricated fallback value and its effect when callers merge parsed tokens into existing credentials.
